Plot saved bias-interaction results

Source: R/api-plotting-dispatch.R
plot.mfrm_bias.Rd

Inspect the pattern of conditional interaction estimates from estimate_bias(). Start with ranked interactions, then use other views to understand the pattern.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_bias'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("scatter", "ranked", "heatmap", "abs_t_hist", "facet_profile"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A result from estimate_bias().

type

"scatter", "ranked", "heatmap", "abs_t_hist", or "facet_profile".

...

Named controls below. draw = FALSE returns the plot data without drawing. Controls do not change the fitted calibration.

Value

An mfrm_plot_data object with view-specific tables, retained screening rules and interpretation notes. Plot agreement across views is not independent evidence of bias. Use print(p) or plot_data(p, "notes") for the interaction definition, score-direction caveat, magnitude-only facet-profile interpretation and conditional uncertainty qualifications outside the figure.

Details

Visualization front-end for bias_interaction_report() with multiple views. With draw = FALSE, the returned plot data include plot_long, plot_annotations, flag_summary, and plot_settings in addition to the view-specific ranked_table, scatter_data, facet_profile, and heatmap components. Use these fields when rebuilding the same screening view in ggplot2, plotly, Quarto, or a dashboard. Saved report thresholds determine flags, reference lines and returned notes; recreate bias_interaction_report() from the saved bias object to change them. Scatter and ranked views support as_ggplot(); the other views require their base renderer or custom graphics. Conditional bounds and their status remain separate from calibration-inclusive uncertainty.

Controls

  • facet_a, facet_b, or interaction_facets identify the interaction; top_n = 40 and sort_by = "abs_t" ("abs_bias" or "prob" also accepted) select ranked interactions.

  • abs_t_warn = 2, abs_bias_warn = 0.5, and p_max = 0.05 set screening rules when preparing a report from the bias result. They are review aids, not guarantees of a calibrated error rate.

  • show_ci = FALSE omits whiskers; ci_level = 0.95 chooses their level for scatter/ranked views. GPCM rows retain conditional profile bounds, with dashed whiskers for search-limited or unverified bounds. Other rows use conditional per-cell SEs. Missing profile bounds are not replaced with another method. These intervals omit calibration uncertainty; endpoint completion is not evidence of coverage.

  • preset selects "standard", "publication", "compact", or "monochrome"; palette overrides named colors (normal, flag, hist, profile); label_angle controls label rotation. title sets title metadata (main is a compatibility alias; supply only one).

Plot types

"scatter" (default)

Observed-minus-expected score average (x) versus conditional bias size in logits (y). Points use the saved flag status; horizontal guides show the saved absolute-bias threshold and zero, with a vertical guide at zero score difference.

"ranked"

Conditional bias size (x) for up to top_n saved ranked interactions (y). Points are colored by flag status; optional whiskers retain the conditional uncertainty and incomplete-bound status. A saved report retains the ranking chosen when it was constructed.

"heatmap"

Facet A by facet B matrix of signed bias size. Cells retain reusable matrix and flag tables for dashboards. This is a Table 13 follow-up display: it supports pattern recognition but does not turn screening rows into confirmatory tests.

"abs_t_hist"

Histogram of absolute screening t-statistics across all interaction cells. Dashed reference line at abs_t_warn. Use for assessing the overall distribution of interaction effect sizes.

"facet_profile"

Per-facet-level aggregation showing mean absolute bias and flag rate. Useful for identifying which individual facet levels drive systematic interaction patterns.

Interpreting output

Start with "scatter" or "ranked" for triage, then confirm pattern shape using "abs_t_hist" and "facet_profile".

These views reuse the same estimates and flags. Agreement between views is not independent corroborating evidence of bias. Review exposure, calibration uncertainty and substantive explanations before drawing conclusions about a rater.

See also

estimate_bias(), bias_interaction_report(), mfrmr_plot_migration, mfrmr_visual_diagnostics

Examples

# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_bias.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "bias-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
diagnostics <- example_fit$diagnostics
bias <- estimate_bias(fit, diagnostics = diagnostics,
  facet_a = "Rater", facet_b = "Criterion")
p <- plot(bias, type = "ranked", preset = "publication", draw = FALSE)
head(plot_data(p, "ranked_table"))
